chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'I manumitted a slave-girl belonging to our orphans, and stipulated with her that if she became unable (to pay), she would be returned to slavery, and I would be free of what I took from you.' He said, 'Your condition is valid. And it will be said to you that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say, "The manumitted slave is freed in proportion to what he has paid of his manumission contract." So say, "That was only from the saying of Ali (peace be upon him) before the people made stipulations; when the people made stipulations, their condition became valid."'

I said to him, 'What is the definition of inability?' He said, 'Our judges say: If the manumitted slave is unable to delay the installment (najm) until the next installment, until a year passes over it.' I said, 'And what do you say?' He said, 'No, and no honor; he is not allowed to delay an installment beyond its appointed time if that is part of his condition.'

key_terms.الشَّرْط: Stipulation or condition agreed upon by the parties.
key_terms.النَّجْم: An installment or periodic payment in the manumission contract.
key_terms.رَدٌّ فِي ٱلرِّقِّ: Return to slavery, implying that if the condition of inability is met, the partial manumission is reversed.
key_terms.عَجْز: Inability or incapacity, specifically regarding the payment of the manumission debt.
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his manumission.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of inability (ajz) in a slave's manumission contract (mukatabah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential evolution regarding *mukatabah*, where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the master's stipulation that failure to pay an installment on time results in a return to slavery, contrasting it with the earlier, more lenient view of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). The text establishes a precise legal definition of 'inability' (*ajz*) as the inability to pay the current installment by its due date, thereby preventing automatic manumission upon partial payment. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contractual stipulations (*shurut*) in commercial and manumission agreements, balancing the rights of the master with the slave's obligation to fulfill the agreed terms strictly.
